1	# Frame Job graphics — the API
2	
3	A **graphic** is a motion graphic drawn by code: one JavaScript ES module
4	whose `render` returns an SVG string for each frame. Frame Job runs it in a
5	sandboxed QuickJS engine and rasterizes the SVG with resvg. The same frame
6	with the same props always draws the same pixels. A gradient is dithered
7	where it is rounded to 8 bits, by a fixed pattern of pixel position under
8	half a level, so dark gradients do not band; flat colours, images, text and
9	alpha are not. This page is the whole API. Every `js` block on it is run
10	by a test, so the examples work as written.
11	
12	## The module
13	
14	```js
15	export const meta = {
16	  name: "Lower third",        // shown in the inspector
17	  durationInFrames: 150,      // optional: the default length of a new clip
18	};
19	
20	export const schema = {
21	  title:    { type: "string",  default: "Jane Doe", label: "Title" },
22	  subtitle: { type: "string",  default: "Director of Photography" },
23	  accent:   { type: "color",   default: "#ff5a36" },
24	  size:     { type: "number",  default: 64, min: 12, max: 200, step: 1 },
25	  boxed:    { type: "boolean", default: true },
26	  align:    { type: "enum",    default: "left", options: ["left", "center", "right"] },
27	};
28	
29	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
30	  const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 20], [-600, 96], { easing: Easing.outCubic, clamp: true });
31	  const fade = interpolate(frame, [ctx.durationInFrames - 15, ctx.durationInFrames - 1], [1, 0],
32	    { clamp: true });
33	  const y = ctx.height - 200;
34	  return svg(ctx, `
35	    <g opacity="${fade}">
36	      ${props.boxed ? `<rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="700" height="150" fill="#101014"/>` : ""}
37	      <rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="12" height="150" fill="${props.accent}"/>
38	      <text x="${x + 40}" y="${y}" font-family="Montserrat" font-weight="800"
39	            font-size="${props.size}" fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(props.title)}</text>
40	    </g>`);
41	}
42	```
43	
44	- `render(frame, props, ctx)` is required. It must return a string that
45	  starts with `<svg`; use `svg(ctx, body)` to write the root element.
46	- `meta` is optional (`{}` when absent). `name` and `durationInFrames` are
47	  read from it.
48	- `schema` is optional (`{}` when absent). It declares the props (below).
49	- The module is the only source of code: no `import`, no `eval`, no
50	  `Function`. The standard library below is already global.
51	- `frame` is an integer counted from the clip's first frame.
52	
53	## `ctx`
54	
55	| key | what |
56	|---|---|
57	| `fps` | the project's frame rate, e.g. `30` or `29.97002997` |
58	| `time` | `frame / fps`, in seconds |
59	| `durationInFrames` | the clip's length in frames |
60	| `progress` | `frame / max(1, durationInFrames - 1)`, clamped to 0–1 |
61	| `width`, `height` | the graphic's size in pixels |
62	| `canvas` | `{width, height}`, the project's canvas |
63	
64	Write every coordinate in terms of `ctx.width` and `ctx.height` (or a unit
65	such as `const u = ctx.height / 1080`) so the graphic draws at any size.
66	
67	## The schema
68	
69	At most 64 keys. A key is letters, digits and `_`, starts with a letter or
70	`_`, and is at most 32 characters. Every entry needs a `type` and a
71	`default` of that type; `label` (else the key) and `help` (a tooltip) are
72	optional. Any entry may say `animate: false` (a boolean; absent is `true`):
73	an action never animates that prop, and the inspector writes it to the clip
74	even while an action is selected — for a count, a layout mode or a data
75	series a ramp would break.
76	
77	| `type` | value | options |
78	|---|---|---|
79	| `string` | text, at most 4096 characters | `multiline: true` for a text area |
80	| `number` | a finite number | `min`, `max`, `step` |
81	| `boolean` | `true` / `false` | |
82	| `color` | a CSS colour string: `"#ff5a36"`, `"rgb(255, 90, 54)"`, `"hsl(11, 100%, 61%)"`, `"tomato"` | |
83	| `enum` | one of `options` | `options`: 1–32 strings |
84	| `asset` | a file name in `graphics/assets/`, `null` or `""` (no image); `render` gets `null` for either of the last two | `kind: "image"` |
85	
86	A schema that breaks a rule does not compile, and the error says which rule.
87	A `color` entry's `default` must be a colour in the grammar
88	`interpolateColors` lists below, or the module does not compile:
89	`schema.accent.default "bluish" is not a color`. `props` receives the
90	default as written, not normalised.
91	`props` always has every schema key: a stored value replaces the default
92	only when it fits the type. A value that does not fit is a WARNING, the
93	default is drawn, and the frame still draws, e.g.
94	`props.size is a string but the schema says number; the default 64 is used`.
95	
96	## The standard library
97	
98	### `svg(ctx, body, {background})`
99	
100	The root element with the right `width`, `height` and `viewBox`.
101	
102	```js
103	const plain = svg(ctx, `<circle cx="100" cy="100" r="50" fill="#fff"/>`);
104	const onBlack = svg(ctx, "", { background: "#000000" });
105	```
106	
107	### `interpolate(value, input, output, {easing, clamp, extrapolateLeft, extrapolateRight})`
108	
109	Maps `value` through matching `input` and `output` ranges (two or more
110	points, `input` ascending). Outside `input` it extends the end segment
111	unless `clamp: true`; `extrapolateLeft` / `extrapolateRight` take
112	`"extend"`, `"clamp"` or `"identity"`.
113	
114	```js
115	const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 30], [0, 400], { clamp: true });
116	const pulse = interpolate(frame, [0, 15, 30], [1, 1.2, 1], { easing: Easing.inOutSine });
117	```
118	
119	### `Easing`
120	
121	`Easing.linear`, `Easing.bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)`, and `in`, `out` and `inOut`
122	of `quad`, `cubic`, `quart`, `expo`, `sine`, `back` and `elastic`, spelled
123	`Easing.inQuad`, `Easing.outCubic`, `Easing.inOutBack` and so on. Each takes
124	`t` in 0–1 and is exact at 0 and 1.
125	
126	```js
127	const eased = Easing.outCubic(0.5);
128	const custom = Easing.bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1)(0.5);
129	const y = interpolate(frame, [0, 20], [300, 0], { easing: Easing.outBack, clamp: true });
130	```
131	
132	### `spring({frame, fps, stiffness = 100, damping = 10, mass = 1, from = 0, to = 1})`
133	
134	A physical spring from `from` to `to`, starting at frame 0 (use
135	`frame - delay` to start later). It overshoots unless damped. The same frame
136	always answers the same value.
137	
138	```js
139	const scale = spring({ frame, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 14 });
140	const late = spring({ frame: frame - 12, fps: ctx.fps, stiffness: 180, from: 0.5, to: 1 });
141	```
142	
143	### `interpolateColors(value, input, colors)`
144	
145	Blends colours in OKLab and answers `#rrggbb` (or `#rrggbbaa` when a colour
146	has alpha). Clamped outside `input`. A colour is `#rgb`, `#rgba`, `#rrggbb`,
147	`#rrggbbaa`, `rgb()` / `rgba()` (channels 0–255 or a percentage, alpha 0–1
148	or a percentage), `hsl()` / `hsla()` (hue in degrees, saturation and
149	lightness percentages), or one of the 147 CSS colour names or
150	`transparent` — the same colours a `color` prop takes. A value out of range
151	(`rgb(300, 0, 0)`) throws rather than being clamped.
152	
153	```js
154	const fill = interpolateColors(frame, [0, 60], ["#ff5a36", "#3666ff"]);
155	const glass = interpolateColors(ctx.progress, [0, 1], ["rgba(255, 255, 255, 0)", "#ffffff"]);
156	const sky = interpolateColors(ctx.progress, [0, 1], ["hsl(200, 80%, 30%)", "skyblue"]);
157	```
158	
159	### `random(seed)`
160	
161	A number in [0, 1) that depends only on `seed` (a number or a string).
162	`Math.random` does not exist in a graphic; this replaces it.
163	
164	```js
165	const jitter = random(`dot-${frame}`) * 10;
166	const hue = Math.floor(random(42) * 360);
167	```
168	
169	### `noise2D(seed, x, y)` and `noise3D(seed, x, y, z)`
170	
171	Simplex noise in about −1..1. Use `noise3D` with time as the third axis for
172	smooth drift.
173	
174	```js
175	const drift = noise2D("wave", frame / 60, 0) * 40;
176	const wobble = noise3D(7, 0.5, 0.5, ctx.time) * 20;
177	```
178	
179	### Paths: `getLength(d)`, `getPointAtLength(d, length)` and `evolvePath(progress, d)`
180	
181	`d` is SVG path data: every command (`M L H V C S Q T A Z`) and its
182	relative form. `getLength` answers the path's length, curves and arcs
183	measured to within about 0.01 %. `getPointAtLength` answers `{x, y, angle}`:
184	the point that far along the path (`length` is clamped to the path) and the
185	way the path is heading there, in degrees, ready for `rotate()`.
186	`evolvePath` answers `{strokeDasharray, strokeDashoffset}` for a `progress`
187	of 0–1: put both on the `<path>` and it is drawn from its start up to that
188	fraction. Its dash is 0.1 % longer than the measured length, so a closed
189	outline closes at 1.
190	
191	A path of several pieces (more than one `M`) draws them all at once, each
192	from its own start and at the same speed, the longest finishing at 1; pieces
193	drawn one after another are one `<path>` each. A path that cannot be read
194	throws, naming where reading stopped —
195	`getLength: cannot parse the path at character 6: "X 5 5"` — and is never a
196	silent zero. A number too large to do arithmetic with (`1e999`, or a line
197	1e200 long, whose square overflows) is refused in the same sentence, so no
198	answer is ever `Infinity` or `NaN`.
199	
200	The paths a graphic measures are remembered, so the same `d` costs a lookup
201	on later calls and frames — up to 32 paths, and about 50,000 characters and
202	measured pieces between them (a curve is 64 pieces). Past either limit all
203	are forgotten and measured again when next asked for, so with paths that
204	large take every length and point from one before turning to the next.
205	
206	```js
207	const d = `M 200 ${ctx.height / 2} C 600 100 1000 900 1400 ${ctx.height / 2}`;
208	const total = getLength(d);
209	const tip = getPointAtLength(d, total * ctx.progress);
210	const dash = evolvePath(ctx.progress, d);
211	const line = `<path d="${d}" fill="none" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="8"
212	  stroke-dasharray="${dash.strokeDasharray}" stroke-dashoffset="${dash.strokeDashoffset}"/>
213	  <circle cx="${tip.x}" cy="${tip.y}" r="12" fill="#ffcc00"/>`;
214	```
215	
216	### `measureText(text, font)`
217	
218	`font` is `{family, size, weight, style, letterSpacing, xmlSpace}`
219	(defaults Montserrat, 16, 400, `"normal"`, 0, `"default"`). Answers
220	`{width, ascent, descent, lineHeight, inkX, inkWidth}`: `width` is the
221	advance (where the next word starts); `inkX` / `inkWidth` are the drawn
222	glyphs. With `xmlSpace: "default"` runs of spaces collapse as SVG draws
223	them; with `"preserve"` a run of spaces beside a drawn glyph counts, as
224	`xml:space="preserve"` draws it, and any other value throws. Text that is
225	only whitespace measures zero either way. A family that is not installed
226	throws, naming the families that are.
227	
228	```js
229	const m = measureText("Hello", { family: "Montserrat", size: 64, weight: 800 });
230	const boxWidth = m.width + 80;
231	const gap = measureText("a  b", { family: "sans-serif", size: 48, xmlSpace: "preserve" });
232	```
233	
234	### `wrapText(text, maxWidth, font)`
235	
236	Lines that each fit `maxWidth`; a word longer than the width breaks by
237	characters.
238	
239	```js
240	const lines = wrapText("A title long enough to need two lines", 600,
241	  { family: "Source Sans 3", size: 64, weight: 700 });
242	```
243	
244	### `fitText(text, maxWidth, font, {min = 8, max = 400})`
245	
246	The largest whole font size at which `text` fits `maxWidth` on one line.
247	
248	```js
249	const size = fitText("BREAKING", ctx.width - 200, { family: "Anton" }, { max: 300 });
250	```
251	
252	### `textLines(lines, {x, y, lineHeight, anchor, fill, font})`
253	
254	A `<text>` with one `<tspan>` per line, the family QUOTED for you (a CSS
255	generic such as `sans-serif` is written bare, as it must be).
256	`anchor` is `"start"`, `"middle"` or `"end"`; `lineHeight` defaults to
257	1.2 × the size. A font with `xmlSpace: "preserve"` writes
258	`xml:space="preserve"` on the `<text>`, so it draws the spaces `measureText`
259	counted; a `style` of `"italic"` or `"oblique"` and a non-zero
260	`letterSpacing` are written as `font-style` and `letter-spacing`, so it draws
261	the font `wrapText` broke the lines with.
262	
263	```js
264	const font = { family: "Source Sans 3", size: 48, weight: 600 };
265	const body = textLines(wrapText("Two short lines of text", 400, font),
266	  { x: 100, y: 200, anchor: "start", fill: "#ffffff", font });
267	const code = textLines(["let  x = 1;"],
268	  { x: 100, y: 300, font: { family: "monospace", size: 32, xmlSpace: "preserve" } });
269	```
270	
271	### `escapeXml(s)`
272	
273	Escapes `& < > " '` — put every prop you write into markup through it.
274	
275	```js
276	const safe = escapeXml("Tom & Jerry <live>");
277	```
278	
279	### `formatNumber(n, {decimals = 0, separator = ","})`
280	
281	There is no `Intl` in the engine; this groups thousands.
282	
283	```js
284	const label = formatNumber(1234567.891, { decimals: 2 });
285	const plain = formatNumber(Math.round(interpolate(frame, [0, 60], [0, 5000], { clamp: true })));
286	```
287	
288	### `asset(name)`
289	
290	The href for a file in the project's `graphics/assets/` folder, for
291	`<image href="…">`. A name that is not there is a warning naming the files
292	that are; the image then does not draw.
293	
294	An asset's name must not start with `.` or `#`, must hold none of
295	`/ : " ' < > &` and no control character, and is at most 247 bytes. A
296	picture added under any other name is renamed as it is copied in —
297	`#logo&mark.png` becomes `logo-mark.png`, then `logo-mark-2.png` if that is
298	taken — and you are told the name to use. A file put in the folder by hand
299	under such a name is skipped, with a warning.
300	
301	```js
302	const logo = `<image href="${asset("logo.png")}" x="40" y="40" width="200" height="200"/>`;
303	```
304	
305	## Fonts
306	
307	A graphic draws with the fonts bundled with Frame Job, plus any `.ttf` /
308	`.otf` in the project's `graphics/fonts/`. Never the system's.
309	
310	| family | weights |
311	|---|---|
312	| Anton | 400 |
313	| Bebas Neue | 400 |
314	| Darker Grotesque | variable, 300–900 |
315	| IBM Plex Mono | 400, 500 |
316	| Montserrat | 800, 900 |
317	| Source Sans 3 | variable, 200–900 |
318	| Source Serif 4 | variable, 200–900 |
319	
320	The CSS generic families draw in bundled faces: `serif` is Source Serif 4,
321	`sans-serif` is Source Sans 3 and `monospace` is IBM Plex Mono. Write a
322	generic unquoted (`font-family="sans-serif"`); quoted, it names a family
323	called "sans-serif", which is not installed. `cursive` and `fantasy` are not
324	installed.
325	
326	**Quote a family** in `font-family` or the `font` shorthand when any word
327	of it starts with a digit: `font-family="'Source Sans 3'"`,
328	`font: 48px 'Source Sans 3'`. Unquoted, `Source Sans 3` is not a
329	valid family list: it draws nothing, with a warning. `textLines` quotes
330	for you. A family the set lacks draws nothing, with a warning naming the
331	families that are installed; in a list (`"Nope, Montserrat"`) the first
332	installed family draws.
333	
334	## The sandbox
335	
336	A graphic is a pure function of `frame`, `props`, `ctx` and its fonts and
337	assets. These refuse, with these sentences:
338	
339	```text
340	Math.random()        → Math.random is not available; use random(seed)
341	import x from "x"    → imports are not available in a graphic; the standard library is global
342	new Function("…")    → Function is not available in a graphic; the module is the one source of code
343	eval("…")            → ReferenceError: eval is not defined
344	```
345	
346	`Date` is frozen: `Date.now()` is `946684800000` and `new Date()` is
347	2000-01-01T00:00:00Z. There is no `fetch`, file, clock, `performance`,
348	`WebAssembly` or `Intl`. Modern syntax works: template literals, `??`, `?.`,
349	`**`, destructuring, `Array.prototype.at`, `replaceAll`, `findLast`.
350	
351	## Limits
352	
353	- **Time**: each call has a budget — 250 ms per frame in preview, 2 s in an
354	  export. The module's top level has one too. Over it, the answer is an
355	  error such as `over the 250 ms budget at frame 12 (InternalError:
356	  interrupted)`.
357	- **Memory**: 64 MB of heap and 1 MB of stack per engine. Past either is an
358	  error with a line and column.
359	- **Size**: a graphic draws at most 8192 pixels on a side.
360	- **The answer**: `render` must return an SVG string. `undefined` is
361	  ``render returned undefined at frame 12 — did you forget `return`?``.
362	  The string may be at most 8 MiB (8388608 bytes); a longer one is
363	  `render returned 9000000 bytes at frame 12; the SVG may be at most
364	  8388608 bytes`.
365	
366	## Diagnostics
367	
368	Every problem comes back as `{level, message, line, column, frame}`.
369	`level` is `"error"` (nothing drew) or `"warning"` (it drew anyway).
370	`line` and `column` are the module's own, when known; for a timeout they
371	are where the function begins, not the statement that ran long. `frame` is
372	set for a problem found while drawing. A warning from the module's top level
373	(such as `asset("x")` outside `render`) has no frame, and comes back with the
374	module's compile: `ok` is still `true`.
375	
376	## Working over MCP
377	
378	Read `graphic_reference` once. `write_graphic {name, source}` answers `ok` and
379	`diagnostics`: write again until `ok` is true. `render_graphic {name, frames}`
380	draws up to 16 frames on a contact sheet with no clip, at most 134217728
381	pixels of frames in all (two at 8192×8192, or sixteen at 3840×2160);
382	`add_graphic_clip {name}` places it, `render_frame` shows a frame,
383	`set_graphic {patch: {props}}` changes it.
384	`paste_attributes {clips, payload, groups: ["graphic"]}` copies one clip's props onto other clips
385	drawn by the same module. `import_graphic_font {path}` answers `families`, the exact names
386	`font-family` must say; `import_graphic_asset {path}` adds a picture for
387	`asset(name)`; its `name` is the one to use, and `renamed_from` says it was
388	renamed. `get_graphic` reads a module or names the folder, which your file
389	tools may edit too; its `API.md` is this page, `API.d.ts` its types.
390	`get_graphic {}`'s `warnings` says what the folder's scan skipped or could
391	not watch, such as a file whose name is not a module name. The app keeps the
392	last 10 texts of each module whenever it sees one replaced: `kept`, in
393	`write_graphic`'s and `get_graphic {name}`'s answers, lists their revisions,
394	newest first, and `get_graphic {}`'s `history` lists every name with a kept
395	text, deleted modules included. `restore_graphic {name, revision?}` writes a
396	kept text back (the newest by default) and keeps the one it replaced.
397	`delete_graphic {name}` removes a module no clip draws and keeps its text, so
398	`restore_graphic` brings it back. `rename_graphic {name, to}` renames a
399	module and repoints every clip that draws it as one undo step; undo renames
400	the file back. The folder's `history/` is the app's: leave it to those three
401	tools. A successful
402	`export` answers `graphic_warnings`, each distinct warning a graphic gave
403	while the file was drawn, with its name and frame.
404	
405	## Animating a prop from the timeline
406	
407	A graphic clip's props can be the target of an action, as a clip's position or opacity can:
408	`add_action {clip, at, duration}` makes the span, and `set_action_end {clip, action, patch:
409	{graphic: {props: {…}}}}` names the values the props end at. Each value is checked against your
410	schema as `set_graphic` checks it, `min` and `max` included, using the module as it is now. Across
411	the action a `number` and a `color` ramp along its curve, a `color` in OKLab, giving the same middle
412	`interpolateColors` gives; a `string`, `boolean` and `enum` change to the end's value when the
413	action ends, and an `asset` changes to the end's image when the action ends, `""` naming no image
414	there (a `null` stops animating the prop); a prop whose entry says `animate: false` cannot be
415	animated (`set_action_end` refuses a value for it). A prop the clip holds no value
416	for starts from the schema's `default` as it is when an action first names it, and that value is
417	written into the clip, so a later change to the default does not move the animation; an asset
418	whose default is `null` starts from `""`. `render` gets
419	that frame's values every frame, and your own animation from `frame` still runs on top. A `null`
420	for a prop in `set_action_end`'s patch stops animating it.
421	
422	**An animated number arrives with decimals**: 64 to 129 is 96.5 halfway, never rounded and never
423	snapped to `step`. A module that needs a whole number rounds it itself, or marks the prop
424	`animate: false` so no action ramps it. One that does neither —
425	`new Array(props.count)` is the usual case — throws on a fraction, so those frames draw the error
426	card, and an export stops there.
427	
428	```js
429	export const meta = { name: "Bars", durationInFrames: 90 };
430	export const schema = {
431	  count: { type: "number", default: 5, min: 1, max: 20, step: 1 },
432	  accent: { type: "color", default: "#ff5a36" },
433	};
434	
435	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
436	  const n = Math.round(props.count);
437	  const w = ctx.width / (2 * n);
438	  let bars = "";
439	  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
440	    bars += `<rect x="${(2 * i + 0.5) * w}" y="${ctx.height / 3}" width="${w}"
441	      height="${ctx.height / 3}" fill="${props.accent}"/>`;
442	  }
443	  return svg(ctx, bars);
444	}
445	```
446	
447	A colour blends in OKLab with straight alpha, exactly as `interpolateColors` blends it: `#ff0000`
448	to `#0000ff` is `#8c53a2` halfway, not the muddy `#800080` of a channel-by-channel blend, and
449	`#ffffff` to `#00000000` is `#63636380`, grey and half transparent. While a prop
450	moves, every frame is drawn anew, so a graphic that had settled costs a full draw per frame for the
451	length of the action.
452	
453	## Video inside a graphic: the matte
454	
455	A graphic cannot read a video's pixels. To show video inside a shape the graphic draws, put the
456	graphic on the track directly above the video and switch that track to a **matte**: Track ▸ Matte
457	in the app, or `set_track {track, matte}` over MCP. A matte track's clips are never drawn. What
458	they show cuts the track directly behind: with `alpha`, the video shows where the graphic is
459	opaque; with `alpha_inverted`, where it is transparent; with `luma` and `luma_inverted`, by the
460	brightness of what it draws. `matte: "none"` turns it off. Where the matte track has no clip, the
461	video shows uncut. The module is written and called exactly as anywhere else. Fill the window in
462	white so it works in every mode, and animate it as usual: the cut follows each frame.
463	
464	```js
465	export const meta = { name: "Window", durationInFrames: 90 };
466	export const schema = { radius: { type: "number", default: 24, min: 0, max: 200 } };
467	
468	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
469	  const t = spring({ frame, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 18 });
470	  const w = ctx.width * 0.6 * t;
471	  const h = ctx.height * 0.6 * t;
472	  return svg(ctx, `<rect x="${(ctx.width - w) / 2}" y="${(ctx.height - h) / 2}"
473	    width="${w}" height="${h}" rx="${props.radius}" fill="#ffffff"/>`);
474	}
475	```
476	
477	On a matte track a clip's position, scale, opacity, crop and actions still shape the window. Its
478	blend mode, drop shadow and reflection do nothing. The matted video's own drop shadow follows the
479	cut-out shape.
480	
481	## Idioms
482	
483	### A slide-in
484	
485	```js
486	export const meta = { name: "Slide in", durationInFrames: 90 };
487	export const schema = { text: { type: "string", default: "Hello" } };
488	
489	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
490	  const u = ctx.height / 1080;
491	  const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 18], [-ctx.width / 2, ctx.width / 2],
492	    { easing: Easing.outCubic, clamp: true });
493	  return svg(ctx, `<text x="${x}" y="${ctx.height / 2}" text-anchor="middle"
494	    font-family="Montserrat" font-weight="800" font-size="${120 * u}"
495	    fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(props.text)}</text>`);
496	}
497	```
498	
499	### A staggered list
500	
501	```js
502	export const meta = { name: "Agenda" };
503	export const schema = {
504	  items: { type: "string", default: "Intro\nDemo\nQuestions", multiline: true, animate: false },
505	  accent: { type: "color", default: "#ffcc00" },
506	};
507	
508	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
509	  const u = ctx.height / 1080;
510	  const rows = props.items.split("\n").filter((s) => s.trim()).map((item, i) => {
511	    const t = spring({ frame: frame - i * 6, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 16 });
512	    const y = 300 * u + i * 110 * u;
513	    return `<g opacity="${Math.min(1, t)}" transform="translate(${(1 - t) * 80 * u} 0)">
514	      <rect x="${160 * u}" y="${y - 50 * u}" width="${14 * u}" height="${64 * u}" fill="${props.accent}"/>
515	      <text x="${200 * u}" y="${y}" font-family="'Source Sans 3'" font-weight="600"
516	        font-size="${64 * u}" fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(item)}</text></g>`;
517	  });
518	  return svg(ctx, rows.join(""));
519	}
520	```
521	
522	### A counter
523	
524	```js
525	export const meta = { name: "Counter", durationInFrames: 120 };
526	export const schema = {
527	  to: { type: "number", default: 25000, min: 0 },
528	  suffix: { type: "string", default: " views" },
529	};
530	
531	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
532	  const value = interpolate(frame, [0, 60], [0, props.to], { easing: Easing.outExpo, clamp: true });
533	  const text = formatNumber(Math.round(value)) + props.suffix;
534	  return svg(ctx, `<text x="${ctx.width / 2}" y="${ctx.height / 2}" text-anchor="middle"
535	    font-family="'IBM Plex Mono'" font-weight="500" font-size="${ctx.height / 8}"
536	    fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(text)}</text>`);
537	}
538	```
539	
540	### Fit and wrap a title
541	
542	```js
543	export const meta = { name: "Title card" };
544	export const schema = {
545	  title: { type: "string", default: "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog" },
546	};
547	
548	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
549	  const maxWidth = ctx.width * 0.8;
550	  const base = { family: "Bebas Neue", weight: 400 };
551	  const size = fitText(props.title, maxWidth * 2, base, { min: 48, max: 220 });
552	  const font = Object.assign({}, base, { size });
553	  const lines = wrapText(props.title, maxWidth, font);
554	  const top = ctx.height / 2 - (lines.length - 1) * size * 0.6;
555	  const fade = interpolate(frame, [0, 12], [0, 1], { clamp: true });
556	  return svg(ctx, `<g opacity="${fade}">${textLines(lines,
557	    { x: ctx.width / 2, y: top, anchor: "middle", fill: "#ffffff", font })}</g>`,
558	    { background: "#16161a" });
559	}
560	```
561	
562	### A draw-on stroke
563	
564	`evolvePath` measures the path and answers the dash that draws it up to a
565	progress of 0–1.
566	
567	```js
568	export const meta = { name: "Underline", durationInFrames: 60 };
569	export const schema = { color: { type: "color", default: "#ff5a36" } };
570	
571	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
572	  const y = ctx.height * 0.62;
573	  const d = `M ${ctx.width * 0.2} ${y} q ${ctx.width * 0.3} ${ctx.height * 0.05} ${ctx.width * 0.6} 0`;
574	  const drawn = interpolate(frame, [0, 24], [0, 1], { easing: Easing.inOutCubic, clamp: true });
575	  const dash = evolvePath(drawn, d);
576	  return svg(ctx, `<path d="${d}" stroke="${props.color}"
577	    stroke-width="${ctx.height / 90}" stroke-linecap="round" fill="none"
578	    stroke-dasharray="${dash.strokeDasharray}" stroke-dashoffset="${dash.strokeDashoffset}"/>`);
579	}
580	```
581	
582	### Follow a path
583	
584	`getPointAtLength` answers where the path is and which way it is heading;
585	`rotate(angle)` turns an arrowhead drawn pointing right to match.
586	
587	```js
588	export const meta = { name: "Arrow", durationInFrames: 60 };
589	export const schema = { color: { type: "color", default: "#ffffff" } };
590	
591	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
592	  const w = ctx.width;
593	  const h = ctx.height;
594	  const d = `M ${w * 0.2} ${h * 0.7} C ${w * 0.4} ${h * 0.2} ${w * 0.6} ${h * 0.2} ${w * 0.8} ${h * 0.5}`;
595	  const drawn = interpolate(frame, [0, 30], [0, 1], { easing: Easing.inOutCubic, clamp: true });
596	  const dash = evolvePath(drawn, d);
597	  const tip = getPointAtLength(d, getLength(d) * drawn);
598	  const s = h / 36;
599	  return svg(ctx, `<path d="${d}" stroke="${props.color}" stroke-width="${h / 120}" fill="none"
600	    stroke-dasharray="${dash.strokeDasharray}" stroke-dashoffset="${dash.strokeDashoffset}"/>
601	    <path d="M ${-s} ${-s * 0.6} L ${s * 0.5} 0 L ${-s} ${s * 0.6} Z" fill="${props.color}"
602	    transform="translate(${tip.x} ${tip.y}) rotate(${tip.angle})"/>`);
603	}
604	```
605

# Frame Job graphics — the API

A **graphic** is a motion graphic drawn by code: one JavaScript ES module
whose `render` returns an SVG string for each frame. Frame Job runs it in a
sandboxed QuickJS engine and rasterizes the SVG with resvg. The same frame
with the same props always draws the same pixels. A gradient is dithered
where it is rounded to 8 bits, by a fixed pattern of pixel position under
half a level, so dark gradients do not band; flat colours, images, text and
alpha are not. This page is the whole API. Every `js` block on it is run
by a test, so the examples work as written.

## The module

```js
export const meta = {
  name: "Lower third",        // shown in the inspector
  durationInFrames: 150,      // optional: the default length of a new clip
};

export const schema = {
  title:    { type: "string",  default: "Jane Doe", label: "Title" },
  subtitle: { type: "string",  default: "Director of Photography" },
  accent:   { type: "color",   default: "#ff5a36" },
  size:     { type: "number",  default: 64, min: 12, max: 200, step: 1 },
  boxed:    { type: "boolean", default: true },
  align:    { type: "enum",    default: "left", options: ["left", "center", "right"] },
};

export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
  const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 20], [-600, 96], { easing: Easing.outCubic, clamp: true });
  const fade = interpolate(frame, [ctx.durationInFrames - 15, ctx.durationInFrames - 1], [1, 0],
    { clamp: true });
  const y = ctx.height - 200;
  return svg(ctx, `
    <g opacity="${fade}">
      ${props.boxed ? `<rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="700" height="150" fill="#101014"/>` : ""}
      <rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="12" height="150" fill="${props.accent}"/>
      <text x="${x + 40}" y="${y}" font-family="Montserrat" font-weight="800"
            font-size="${props.size}" fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(props.title)}</text>
    </g>`);
}
```

- `render(frame, props, ctx)` is required. It must return a string that
  starts with `<svg`; use `svg(ctx, body)` to write the root element.
- `meta` is optional (`{}` when absent). `name` and `durationInFrames` are
  read from it.
- `schema` is optional (`{}` when absent). It declares the props (below).
- The module is the only source of code: no `import`, no `eval`, no
  `Function`. The standard library below is already global.
- `frame` is an integer counted from the clip's first frame.

## `ctx`

| key | what |
|---|---|
| `fps` | the project's frame rate, e.g. `30` or `29.97002997` |
| `time` | `frame / fps`, in seconds |
| `durationInFrames` | the clip's length in frames |
| `progress` | `frame / max(1, durationInFrames - 1)`, clamped to 0–1 |
| `width`, `height` | the graphic's size in pixels |
| `canvas` | `{width, height}`, the project's canvas |

Write every coordinate in terms of `ctx.width` and `ctx.height` (or a unit
such as `const u = ctx.height / 1080`) so the graphic draws at any size.

## The schema

At most 64 keys. A key is letters, digits and `_`, starts with a letter or
`_`, and is at most 32 characters. Every entry needs a `type` and a
`default` of that type; `label` (else the key) and `help` (a tooltip) are
optional. Any entry may say `animate: false` (a boolean; absent is `true`):
an action never animates that prop, and the inspector writes it to the clip
even while an action is selected — for a count, a layout mode or a data
series a ramp would break.

| `type` | value | options |
|---|---|---|
| `string` | text, at most 4096 characters | `multiline: true` for a text area |
| `number` | a finite number | `min`, `max`, `step` |
| `boolean` | `true` / `false` | |
| `color` | a CSS colour string: `"#ff5a36"`, `"rgb(255, 90, 54)"`, `"hsl(11, 100%, 61%)"`, `"tomato"` | |
| `enum` | one of `options` | `options`: 1–32 strings |
| `asset` | a file name in `graphics/assets/`, `null` or `""` (no image); `render` gets `null` for either of the last two | `kind: "image"` |

A schema that breaks a rule does not compile, and the error says which rule.
A `color` entry's `default` must be a colour in the grammar
`interpolateColors` lists below, or the module does not compile:
`schema.accent.default "bluish" is not a color`. `props` receives the
default as written, not normalised.
`props` always has every schema key: a stored value replaces the default
only when it fits the type. A value that does not fit is a WARNING, the
default is drawn, and the frame still draws, e.g.
`props.size is a string but the schema says number; the default 64 is used`.

## The standard library

### `svg(ctx, body, {background})`

The root element with the right `width`, `height` and `viewBox`.

```js
const plain = svg(ctx, `<circle cx="100" cy="100" r="50" fill="#fff"/>`);
const onBlack = svg(ctx, "", { background: "#000000" });
```

### `interpolate(value, input, output, {easing, clamp, extrapolateLeft, extrapolateRight})`

Maps `value` through matching `input` and `output` ranges (two or more
points, `input` ascending). Outside `input` it extends the end segment
unless `clamp: true`; `extrapolateLeft` / `extrapolateRight` take
`"extend"`, `"clamp"` or `"identity"`.

```js
const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 30], [0, 400], { clamp: true });
const pulse = interpolate(frame, [0, 15, 30], [1, 1.2, 1], { easing: Easing.inOutSine });
```

### `Easing`

`Easing.linear`, `Easing.bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)`, and `in`, `out` and `inOut`
of `quad`, `cubic`, `quart`, `expo`, `sine`, `back` and `elastic`, spelled
`Easing.inQuad`, `Easing.outCubic`, `Easing.inOutBack` and so on. Each takes
`t` in 0–1 and is exact at 0 and 1.

```js
const eased = Easing.outCubic(0.5);
const custom = Easing.bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1)(0.5);
const y = interpolate(frame, [0, 20], [300, 0], { easing: Easing.outBack, clamp: true });
```

### `spring({frame, fps, stiffness = 100, damping = 10, mass = 1, from = 0, to = 1})`

A physical spring from `from` to `to`, starting at frame 0 (use
`frame - delay` to start later). It overshoots unless damped. The same frame
always answers the same value.

```js
const scale = spring({ frame, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 14 });
const late = spring({ frame: frame - 12, fps: ctx.fps, stiffness: 180, from: 0.5, to: 1 });
```

### `interpolateColors(value, input, colors)`

Blends colours in OKLab and answers `#rrggbb` (or `#rrggbbaa` when a colour
has alpha). Clamped outside `input`. A colour is `#rgb`, `#rgba`, `#rrggbb`,
`#rrggbbaa`, `rgb()` / `rgba()` (channels 0–255 or a percentage, alpha 0–1
or a percentage), `hsl()` / `hsla()` (hue in degrees, saturation and
lightness percentages), or one of the 147 CSS colour names or
`transparent` — the same colours a `color` prop takes. A value out of range
(`rgb(300, 0, 0)`) throws rather than being clamped.

```js
const fill = interpolateColors(frame, [0, 60], ["#ff5a36", "#3666ff"]);
const glass = interpolateColors(ctx.progress, [0, 1], ["rgba(255, 255, 255, 0)", "#ffffff"]);
const sky = interpolateColors(ctx.progress, [0, 1], ["hsl(200, 80%, 30%)", "skyblue"]);
```

### `random(seed)`

A number in [0, 1) that depends only on `seed` (a number or a string).
`Math.random` does not exist in a graphic; this replaces it.

```js
const jitter = random(`dot-${frame}`) * 10;
const hue = Math.floor(random(42) * 360);
```

### `noise2D(seed, x, y)` and `noise3D(seed, x, y, z)`

Simplex noise in about −1..1. Use `noise3D` with time as the third axis for
smooth drift.

```js
const drift = noise2D("wave", frame / 60, 0) * 40;
const wobble = noise3D(7, 0.5, 0.5, ctx.time) * 20;
```

### Paths: `getLength(d)`, `getPointAtLength(d, length)` and `evolvePath(progress, d)`

`d` is SVG path data: every command (`M L H V C S Q T A Z`) and its
relative form. `getLength` answers the path's length, curves and arcs
measured to within about 0.01 %. `getPointAtLength` answers `{x, y, angle}`:
the point that far along the path (`length` is clamped to the path) and the
way the path is heading there, in degrees, ready for `rotate()`.
`evolvePath` answers `{strokeDasharray, strokeDashoffset}` for a `progress`
of 0–1: put both on the `<path>` and it is drawn from its start up to that
fraction. Its dash is 0.1 % longer than the measured length, so a closed
outline closes at 1.

A path of several pieces (more than one `M`) draws them all at once, each
from its own start and at the same speed, the longest finishing at 1; pieces
drawn one after another are one `<path>` each. A path that cannot be read
throws, naming where reading stopped —
`getLength: cannot parse the path at character 6: "X 5 5"` — and is never a
silent zero. A number too large to do arithmetic with (`1e999`, or a line
1e200 long, whose square overflows) is refused in the same sentence, so no
answer is ever `Infinity` or `NaN`.

The paths a graphic measures are remembered, so the same `d` costs a lookup
on later calls and frames — up to 32 paths, and about 50,000 characters and
measured pieces between them (a curve is 64 pieces). Past either limit all
are forgotten and measured again when next asked for, so with paths that
large take every length and point from one before turning to the next.

```js
const d = `M 200 ${ctx.height / 2} C 600 100 1000 900 1400 ${ctx.height / 2}`;
const total = getLength(d);
const tip = getPointAtLength(d, total * ctx.progress);
const dash = evolvePath(ctx.progress, d);
const line = `<path d="${d}" fill="none" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="8"
  stroke-dasharray="${dash.strokeDasharray}" stroke-dashoffset="${dash.strokeDashoffset}"/>
  <circle cx="${tip.x}" cy="${tip.y}" r="12" fill="#ffcc00"/>`;
```

### `measureText(text, font)`

`font` is `{family, size, weight, style, letterSpacing, xmlSpace}`
(defaults Montserrat, 16, 400, `"normal"`, 0, `"default"`). Answers
`{width, ascent, descent, lineHeight, inkX, inkWidth}`: `width` is the
advance (where the next word starts); `inkX` / `inkWidth` are the drawn
glyphs. With `xmlSpace: "default"` runs of spaces collapse as SVG draws
them; with `"preserve"` a run of spaces beside a drawn glyph counts, as
`xml:space="preserve"` draws it, and any other value throws. Text that is
only whitespace measures zero either way. A family that is not installed
throws, naming the families that are.

```js
const m = measureText("Hello", { family: "Montserrat", size: 64, weight: 800 });
const boxWidth = m.width + 80;
const gap = measureText("a  b", { family: "sans-serif", size: 48, xmlSpace: "preserve" });
```

### `wrapText(text, maxWidth, font)`

Lines that each fit `maxWidth`; a word longer than the width breaks by
characters.

```js
const lines = wrapText("A title long enough to need two lines", 600,
  { family: "Source Sans 3", size: 64, weight: 700 });
```

### `fitText(text, maxWidth, font, {min = 8, max = 400})`

The largest whole font size at which `text` fits `maxWidth` on one line.

```js
const size = fitText("BREAKING", ctx.width - 200, { family: "Anton" }, { max: 300 });
```

### `textLines(lines, {x, y, lineHeight, anchor, fill, font})`

A `<text>` with one `<tspan>` per line, the family QUOTED for you (a CSS
generic such as `sans-serif` is written bare, as it must be).
`anchor` is `"start"`, `"middle"` or `"end"`; `lineHeight` defaults to
1.2 × the size. A font with `xmlSpace: "preserve"` writes
`xml:space="preserve"` on the `<text>`, so it draws the spaces `measureText`
counted; a `style` of `"italic"` or `"oblique"` and a non-zero
`letterSpacing` are written as `font-style` and `letter-spacing`, so it draws
the font `wrapText` broke the lines with.

```js
const font = { family: "Source Sans 3", size: 48, weight: 600 };
const body = textLines(wrapText("Two short lines of text", 400, font),
  { x: 100, y: 200, anchor: "start", fill: "#ffffff", font });
const code = textLines(["let  x = 1;"],
  { x: 100, y: 300, font: { family: "monospace", size: 32, xmlSpace: "preserve" } });
```

### `escapeXml(s)`

Escapes `& < > " '` — put every prop you write into markup through it.

```js
const safe = escapeXml("Tom & Jerry <live>");
```

### `formatNumber(n, {decimals = 0, separator = ","})`

There is no `Intl` in the engine; this groups thousands.

```js
const label = formatNumber(1234567.891, { decimals: 2 });
const plain = formatNumber(Math.round(interpolate(frame, [0, 60], [0, 5000], { clamp: true })));
```

### `asset(name)`

The href for a file in the project's `graphics/assets/` folder, for
`<image href="…">`. A name that is not there is a warning naming the files
that are; the image then does not draw.

An asset's name must not start with `.` or `#`, must hold none of
`/ : " ' < > &` and no control character, and is at most 247 bytes. A
picture added under any other name is renamed as it is copied in —
`#logo&mark.png` becomes `logo-mark.png`, then `logo-mark-2.png` if that is
taken — and you are told the name to use. A file put in the folder by hand
under such a name is skipped, with a warning.

```js
const logo = `<image href="${asset("logo.png")}" x="40" y="40" width="200" height="200"/>`;
```

## Fonts

A graphic draws with the fonts bundled with Frame Job, plus any `.ttf` /
`.otf` in the project's `graphics/fonts/`. Never the system's.

| family | weights |
|---|---|
| Anton | 400 |
| Bebas Neue | 400 |
| Darker Grotesque | variable, 300–900 |
| IBM Plex Mono | 400, 500 |
| Montserrat | 800, 900 |
| Source Sans 3 | variable, 200–900 |
| Source Serif 4 | variable, 200–900 |

The CSS generic families draw in bundled faces: `serif` is Source Serif 4,
`sans-serif` is Source Sans 3 and `monospace` is IBM Plex Mono. Write a
generic unquoted (`font-family="sans-serif"`); quoted, it names a family
called "sans-serif", which is not installed. `cursive` and `fantasy` are not
installed.

**Quote a family** in `font-family` or the `font` shorthand when any word
of it starts with a digit: `font-family="'Source Sans 3'"`,
`font: 48px 'Source Sans 3'`. Unquoted, `Source Sans 3` is not a
valid family list: it draws nothing, with a warning. `textLines` quotes
for you. A family the set lacks draws nothing, with a warning naming the
families that are installed; in a list (`"Nope, Montserrat"`) the first
installed family draws.

## The sandbox

A graphic is a pure function of `frame`, `props`, `ctx` and its fonts and
assets. These refuse, with these sentences:

```text
Math.random()        → Math.random is not available; use random(seed)
import x from "x"    → imports are not available in a graphic; the standard library is global
new Function("…")    → Function is not available in a graphic; the module is the one source of code
eval("…")            → ReferenceError: eval is not defined
```

`Date` is frozen: `Date.now()` is `946684800000` and `new Date()` is
2000-01-01T00:00:00Z. There is no `fetch`, file, clock, `performance`,
`WebAssembly` or `Intl`. Modern syntax works: template literals, `??`, `?.`,
`**`, destructuring, `Array.prototype.at`, `replaceAll`, `findLast`.

## Limits

- **Time**: each call has a budget — 250 ms per frame in preview, 2 s in an
  export. The module's top level has one too. Over it, the answer is an
  error such as `over the 250 ms budget at frame 12 (InternalError:
  interrupted)`.
- **Memory**: 64 MB of heap and 1 MB of stack per engine. Past either is an
  error with a line and column.
- **Size**: a graphic draws at most 8192 pixels on a side.
- **The answer**: `render` must return an SVG string. `undefined` is
  ``render returned undefined at frame 12 — did you forget `return`?``.
  The string may be at most 8 MiB (8388608 bytes); a longer one is
  `render returned 9000000 bytes at frame 12; the SVG may be at most
  8388608 bytes`.

## Diagnostics

Every problem comes back as `{level, message, line, column, frame}`.
`level` is `"error"` (nothing drew) or `"warning"` (it drew anyway).
`line` and `column` are the module's own, when known; for a timeout they
are where the function begins, not the statement that ran long. `frame` is
set for a problem found while drawing. A warning from the module's top level
(such as `asset("x")` outside `render`) has no frame, and comes back with the
module's compile: `ok` is still `true`.

## Working over MCP

Read `graphic_reference` once. `write_graphic {name, source}` answers `ok` and
`diagnostics`: write again until `ok` is true. `render_graphic {name, frames}`
draws up to 16 frames on a contact sheet with no clip, at most 134217728
pixels of frames in all (two at 8192×8192, or sixteen at 3840×2160);
`add_graphic_clip {name}` places it, `render_frame` shows a frame,
`set_graphic {patch: {props}}` changes it.
`paste_attributes {clips, payload, groups: ["graphic"]}` copies one clip's props onto other clips
drawn by the same module. `import_graphic_font {path}` answers `families`, the exact names
`font-family` must say; `import_graphic_asset {path}` adds a picture for
`asset(name)`; its `name` is the one to use, and `renamed_from` says it was
renamed. `get_graphic` reads a module or names the folder, which your file
tools may edit too; its `API.md` is this page, `API.d.ts` its types.
`get_graphic {}`'s `warnings` says what the folder's scan skipped or could
not watch, such as a file whose name is not a module name. The app keeps the
last 10 texts of each module whenever it sees one replaced: `kept`, in
`write_graphic`'s and `get_graphic {name}`'s answers, lists their revisions,
newest first, and `get_graphic {}`'s `history` lists every name with a kept
text, deleted modules included. `restore_graphic {name, revision?}` writes a
kept text back (the newest by default) and keeps the one it replaced.
`delete_graphic {name}` removes a module no clip draws and keeps its text, so
`restore_graphic` brings it back. `rename_graphic {name, to}` renames a
module and repoints every clip that draws it as one undo step; undo renames
the file back. The folder's `history/` is the app's: leave it to those three
tools. A successful
`export` answers `graphic_warnings`, each distinct warning a graphic gave
while the file was drawn, with its name and frame.

## Animating a prop from the timeline

A graphic clip's props can be the target of an action, as a clip's position or opacity can:
`add_action {clip, at, duration}` makes the span, and `set_action_end {clip, action, patch:
{graphic: {props: {…}}}}` names the values the props end at. Each value is checked against your
schema as `set_graphic` checks it, `min` and `max` included, using the module as it is now. Across
the action a `number` and a `color` ramp along its curve, a `color` in OKLab, giving the same middle
`interpolateColors` gives; a `string`, `boolean` and `enum` change to the end's value when the
action ends, and an `asset` changes to the end's image when the action ends, `""` naming no image
there (a `null` stops animating the prop); a prop whose entry says `animate: false` cannot be
animated (`set_action_end` refuses a value for it). A prop the clip holds no value
for starts from the schema's `default` as it is when an action first names it, and that value is
written into the clip, so a later change to the default does not move the animation; an asset
whose default is `null` starts from `""`. `render` gets
that frame's values every frame, and your own animation from `frame` still runs on top. A `null`
for a prop in `set_action_end`'s patch stops animating it.

**An animated number arrives with decimals**: 64 to 129 is 96.5 halfway, never rounded and never
snapped to `step`. A module that needs a whole number rounds it itself, or marks the prop
`animate: false` so no action ramps it. One that does neither —
`new Array(props.count)` is the usual case — throws on a fraction, so those frames draw the error
card, and an export stops there.

```js
export const meta = { name: "Bars", durationInFrames: 90 };
export const schema = {
  count: { type: "number", default: 5, min: 1, max: 20, step: 1 },
  accent: { type: "color", default: "#ff5a36" },
};

export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
  const n = Math.round(props.count);
  const w = ctx.width / (2 * n);
  let bars = "";
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    bars += `<rect x="${(2 * i + 0.5) * w}" y="${ctx.height / 3}" width="${w}"
      height="${ctx.height / 3}" fill="${props.accent}"/>`;
  }
  return svg(ctx, bars);
}
```

A colour blends in OKLab with straight alpha, exactly as `interpolateColors` blends it: `#ff0000`
to `#0000ff` is `#8c53a2` halfway, not the muddy `#800080` of a channel-by-channel blend, and
`#ffffff` to `#00000000` is `#63636380`, grey and half transparent. While a prop
moves, every frame is drawn anew, so a graphic that had settled costs a full draw per frame for the
length of the action.

## Video inside a graphic: the matte

A graphic cannot read a video's pixels. To show video inside a shape the graphic draws, put the
graphic on the track directly above the video and switch that track to a **matte**: Track ▸ Matte
in the app, or `set_track {track, matte}` over MCP. A matte track's clips are never drawn. What
they show cuts the track directly behind: with `alpha`, the video shows where the graphic is
opaque; with `alpha_inverted`, where it is transparent; with `luma` and `luma_inverted`, by the
brightness of what it draws. `matte: "none"` turns it off. Where the matte track has no clip, the
video shows uncut. The module is written and called exactly as anywhere else. Fill the window in
white so it works in every mode, and animate it as usual: the cut follows each frame.

```js
export const meta = { name: "Window", durationInFrames: 90 };
export const schema = { radius: { type: "number", default: 24, min: 0, max: 200 } };

export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
  const t = spring({ frame, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 18 });
  const w = ctx.width * 0.6 * t;
  const h = ctx.height * 0.6 * t;
  return svg(ctx, `<rect x="${(ctx.width - w) / 2}" y="${(ctx.height - h) / 2}"
    width="${w}" height="${h}" rx="${props.radius}" fill="#ffffff"/>`);
}
```

On a matte track a clip's position, scale, opacity, crop and actions still shape the window. Its
blend mode, drop shadow and reflection do nothing. The matted video's own drop shadow follows the
cut-out shape.

## Idioms

### A slide-in

```js
export const meta = { name: "Slide in", durationInFrames: 90 };
export const schema = { text: { type: "string", default: "Hello" } };

export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
  const u = ctx.height / 1080;
  const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 18], [-ctx.width / 2, ctx.width / 2],
    { easing: Easing.outCubic, clamp: true });
  return svg(ctx, `<text x="${x}" y="${ctx.height / 2}" text-anchor="middle"
    font-family="Montserrat" font-weight="800" font-size="${120 * u}"
    fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(props.text)}</text>`);
}
```

### A staggered list

```js
export const meta = { name: "Agenda" };
export const schema = {
  items: { type: "string", default: "Intro\nDemo\nQuestions", multiline: true, animate: false },
  accent: { type: "color", default: "#ffcc00" },
};

export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
  const u = ctx.height / 1080;
  const rows = props.items.split("\n").filter((s) => s.trim()).map((item, i) => {
    const t = spring({ frame: frame - i * 6, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 16 });
    const y = 300 * u + i * 110 * u;
    return `<g opacity="${Math.min(1, t)}" transform="translate(${(1 - t) * 80 * u} 0)">
      <rect x="${160 * u}" y="${y - 50 * u}" width="${14 * u}" height="${64 * u}" fill="${props.accent}"/>
      <text x="${200 * u}" y="${y}" font-family="'Source Sans 3'" font-weight="600"
        font-size="${64 * u}" fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(item)}</text></g>`;
  });
  return svg(ctx, rows.join(""));
}
```

### A counter

```js
export const meta = { name: "Counter", durationInFrames: 120 };
export const schema = {
  to: { type: "number", default: 25000, min: 0 },
  suffix: { type: "string", default: " views" },
};

export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
  const value = interpolate(frame, [0, 60], [0, props.to], { easing: Easing.outExpo, clamp: true });
  const text = formatNumber(Math.round(value)) + props.suffix;
  return svg(ctx, `<text x="${ctx.width / 2}" y="${ctx.height / 2}" text-anchor="middle"
    font-family="'IBM Plex Mono'" font-weight="500" font-size="${ctx.height / 8}"
    fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(text)}</text>`);
}
```

### Fit and wrap a title

```js
export const meta = { name: "Title card" };
export const schema = {
  title: { type: "string", default: "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog" },
};

export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
  const maxWidth = ctx.width * 0.8;
  const base = { family: "Bebas Neue", weight: 400 };
  const size = fitText(props.title, maxWidth * 2, base, { min: 48, max: 220 });
  const font = Object.assign({}, base, { size });
  const lines = wrapText(props.title, maxWidth, font);
  const top = ctx.height / 2 - (lines.length - 1) * size * 0.6;
  const fade = interpolate(frame, [0, 12], [0, 1], { clamp: true });
  return svg(ctx, `<g opacity="${fade}">${textLines(lines,
    { x: ctx.width / 2, y: top, anchor: "middle", fill: "#ffffff", font })}</g>`,
    { background: "#16161a" });
}
```

### A draw-on stroke

`evolvePath` measures the path and answers the dash that draws it up to a
progress of 0–1.

```js
export const meta = { name: "Underline", durationInFrames: 60 };
export const schema = { color: { type: "color", default: "#ff5a36" } };

export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
  const y = ctx.height * 0.62;
  const d = `M ${ctx.width * 0.2} ${y} q ${ctx.width * 0.3} ${ctx.height * 0.05} ${ctx.width * 0.6} 0`;
  const drawn = interpolate(frame, [0, 24], [0, 1], { easing: Easing.inOutCubic, clamp: true });
  const dash = evolvePath(drawn, d);
  return svg(ctx, `<path d="${d}" stroke="${props.color}"
    stroke-width="${ctx.height / 90}" stroke-linecap="round" fill="none"
    stroke-dasharray="${dash.strokeDasharray}" stroke-dashoffset="${dash.strokeDashoffset}"/>`);
}
```

### Follow a path

`getPointAtLength` answers where the path is and which way it is heading;
`rotate(angle)` turns an arrowhead drawn pointing right to match.

```js
export const meta = { name: "Arrow", durationInFrames: 60 };
export const schema = { color: { type: "color", default: "#ffffff" } };

export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
  const w = ctx.width;
  const h = ctx.height;
  const d = `M ${w * 0.2} ${h * 0.7} C ${w * 0.4} ${h * 0.2} ${w * 0.6} ${h * 0.2} ${w * 0.8} ${h * 0.5}`;
  const drawn = interpolate(frame, [0, 30], [0, 1], { easing: Easing.inOutCubic, clamp: true });
  const dash = evolvePath(drawn, d);
  const tip = getPointAtLength(d, getLength(d) * drawn);
  const s = h / 36;
  return svg(ctx, `<path d="${d}" stroke="${props.color}" stroke-width="${h / 120}" fill="none"
    stroke-dasharray="${dash.strokeDasharray}" stroke-dashoffset="${dash.strokeDashoffset}"/>
    <path d="M ${-s} ${-s * 0.6} L ${s * 0.5} 0 L ${-s} ${s * 0.6} Z" fill="${props.color}"
    transform="translate(${tip.x} ${tip.y}) rotate(${tip.angle})"/>`);
}
```

2284 11-decisions/graphics.md

- **G-43 — Every colour an action animates blends in OKLab, with
  straight alpha, by key; amends G-40 (d), G-34 (f)** (graphics gaps
  phase 4, 2026-10-22).
  (a) **The keys.** Nine keys of an action's state are colours, known by
  key and never by the value's shape: `video.shadow.color`, `text.color`,
  `text.outline.color`, `text.backdrop.color`,
  `text.word_style.active_color`, `.spoken_color`, `.upcoming_color`,
  `text.word_style.active_pill.color` (each `[r, g, b, a]`, sRGB-encoded
  0–1) and `video.chroma.key` (`[r, g, b]`, no alpha). Inside the spanning
  action each one whose start and end differ moves from its start toward
  its end in OKLab: the inputs clamped to [0, 1], then G-40's operations
  (sRGB → linear → OKLab, a mix by the eased progress, and back) in
  floating point, never rounded to a byte. Alpha is `a0 + (a1 − a0) × u`,
  straight, never premultiplied, clamped to [0, 1]; the chroma key is rgb
  only. A key whose start and end are the same numbers (compared parsed, so
  a stored `1.0` and an end's `1` are equal) is not blended, so it stays
  exactly as stored (the round trip would drift it by ~1e-7). A value that
  does not read as a colour of its key's arity (a `null`, a missing
  group, a wrong length, a non-number) keeps §5.4's rule: it holds and
  switches at the end. The ends are the stored values: an action's first
  tick is its start and its end is its end, exactly. Red to blue halfway
  is `#8c53a2` (×255 rounded), never `[0.5, 0, 0.5]`.
  (b) **One implementation.** `model_color.rs`'s unit path
  (`oklab_mix_unit`, `oklab_mix_rgb`) is the blend; G-40's `oklab_mix`
  is that path with each byte read as byte/255 and each unit rounded to
  the nearest byte, so its output does not change by a byte.
  `graphic/tests/oklab.json` is answered by three readers:
  `graphic/tests/stdlib.rs`, `core/tests/graphic_actions.rs` (bytes), and
  `core/tests/action_colours.rs`, which takes each case's bytes/255 in and
  compares the result ×255 rounded to the fixture.
  (c) **Older projects** re-render with the new middle. No persisted
  shape changes, so `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` is not bumped and there is no
  migration.
  (d) **Not changed.** The `shape` group and `canvas.background` are not
  action targets (§5.4's three groups), so they have no blend; a colour
  plate is a shape. At a `split` the join is exact (`clip_state` either
  side of the cut is equal); inside the head and the tail a sample
  matches the unsplit clip within the matrices' round-trip error (1e-6
  per channel), not exactly.

11-decisions/README.md:234:| G-33 | On an export row that needs even pixel dimensions the core resolves and lists the even size the file will have — an odd edge one pixel smaller, the Document row named "Document (even)" — so the sheet and the `export` tool report the file's size and no size of the canvas's own shape is refused for being odd; `hevc_alpha`, "HEVC with Alpha (MOV)", is a tenth row whose frames carry the canvas's alpha; every movie row fills the frame instead of padding it when the miss is within a pixel or the frame is a canvas-shaped size less a pixel (one integer test, shared with the alpha guard), and letterboxes or, on an alpha row, refuses past that; a missing encoder is the preset's own sentence and no file; `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` stays 11; amended by #243: the export sheet 60 pt wider and its footnote on a line of its own above the buttons, so every footnote measured, the default rows and the longest two, is drawn whole; amended by G-35: the two alpha movie rows are written straight and labelled so, and Frame Job reads a video frame's declared alpha mode | [`graphics.md`](graphics.md) |
11-decisions/README.md:235:| G-34 | A graphic's props are action targets: a number and a colour (in OKLab, straight alpha — amended by G-40) ramp, a string, boolean or enum switches at the end, an asset switches at the end (G-42), and a prop its module marks `animate: false` (G-41) is refused; the kind comes from the schema the op carries and is stored in the end's `kinds` (a caller's `kinds` is discarded); a named prop is range-checked, a stored end never re-checked; a prop the clip lacks starts from the schema's current default, written in the same step, and a paste keeps an animated start (amends G-32 (e)); numbers arrive fractional; `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` 13; supersedes G-10's first sentence | [`graphics.md`](graphics.md) |
11-decisions/README.md:236:| G-35 | A video frame is composited as premultiplied only when its buffer's alpha-mode attachment says `PremultipliedAlpha`, an unlabelled one as straight; `prores_4444` and `hevc_alpha` are written straight — each frame un-premultiplied in integers (exact for 8 bits), each transparent pixel within 4 px of a visible one filled with the nearest one's colour, every buffer labelled `StraightAlpha` and `hevc_alpha`'s encoder key straight; `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` unchanged, no migration (the owner's "do both", #242); amends G-33 (d) and (h); amended by PR-3 (`prores_4444` un-premultiplied in float, `hevc_alpha` rounded to 8 bits first) — amended by CX-17 (`vp9_alpha_webm` straightened in float too) | [`graphics.md`](graphics.md) |
11-decisions/README.md:237:| G-36 | Playback rasterizes upcoming graphic frames ahead on worker threads too, on the document's key while playing forward with a graphic clip; a session starts at the seek target or the playhead on the composition's grid and restarts on play, seek, item swap and a property edit while playing; workers follow the compositor's reached frame, counting `skipped`; G-26's bounds per session until #127's next phase replaces them with 25 % of physical memory (the owner's choice: no fixed limit) and a setting for drawing ahead while paused; the compositor stays the one consumer and the texture key decides; amends G-26 (a) — amended by G-37 — amended by G-38 | [`graphics.md`](graphics.md) |
11-decisions/README.md:238:| G-37 | Graphic rasters share one memory budget, a quarter of physical memory, over every session's held rasters and the kept frames, under 1,024 entries per session; memory pressure halves it (warning) or zeroes it (critical); a document's playback keeps the graphic frames it drew under their texture keys, served on a pool miss before any slot and dropped when the window closes; `FrameJobGraphicKeepOff` keeps nothing; amends G-26 (d) and G-36 (e) — amended by G-38 — amended by G-39 | [`graphics.md`](graphics.md) |
11-decisions/README.md:239:| G-38 | Graphic frames are drawn ahead while paused once the person has left Frame Job alone (Settings ▸ Playback ▸ Background render, on after 5 s by default, as Final Cut's; a person's setting with no tool): any key, click, drag, scroll or gesture, any edit and any transport move restarts the clock and stops the pass; the document whose transport last moved, paused, built and drawing a graphic, draws from its playhead at utility QoS into its kept frames, marked as drawn ahead, which give way last and which a play from the pass's start does not push out; one pass at a time, never beside any window's play, Frame Job opted out of App Nap for its life; ends `done`, `full` or `stopped`; amends G-36 (a) and G-37 (c). Measured on parive-promo's `section` scene (Release, Full, 10 s from tick 25 120 000, 12 cores, 96 GiB, `powermode 0`, 2026-10-21): 0.292 of its frames composed with Background render off (load average 31.8 before the play), 1.0 after a `full` pass (3,103 rasters, 25.8 GB kept; load average 87.1; measured on the code before fix pass 1, whose bench was cut short by host activity) | [`graphics.md`](graphics.md) |
11-decisions/README.md:240:| G-39 | A graphic's PNG and JPEG assets are kept as stored PNG copies that decode to the same pixmap, in one process-wide cache keyed by content and sized from G-37's budget: the straight RGBA8 written as a stored, unfiltered RGBA PNG on the first frame that draws it, used only when it decodes to the original's pixmap at the original's size; keyed by the SHA-256 of the asset's bytes; its limit `budgetBytes / 16` at the level in force (physical/64 at normal, physical/128 at warning, 0 at critical), trimmed least recently used first; a copy that does not fit is remembered by its size and drawn the original way until there is room, so nothing is rebuilt per frame; `FrameJobGraphicImageCacheOff` sets 0; amends G-37. Measured on parive-promo's `section` scene (40 frames of 1920 × 1080, 5 rounds, load average 6.10, `powermode 0`, 2026-10-22): a saving of 0.0429 against a spread of 0.0330 | [`graphics.md`](graphics.md) |
11-decisions/README.md:241:| G-40 | An action on a graphic `color` prop blends in OKLab, as stdlib's `interpolateColors` does, with straight alpha; no setting and no per-action or per-end key; one fixture, `graphic/tests/oklab.json`, both answer; no format bump, no migration; amends G-34 (f) — amended by G-43 | [`graphics.md`](graphics.md) |
11-decisions/README.md:242:| G-41 | A schema entry's optional boolean `animate: false` (any type) means no action animates the prop: `set_action_end` refuses a non-null value for it by name, after an unknown key, a `null` still removing; a non-boolean `animate` is refused by the engine and the core in one sentence; a stored end is not re-checked, and the Graphic tab lists such a key as the end's stale row; with an action selected the row is ⊘ and writes `set_graphic`; no format bump; amends G-34 (b), (l) and its accepted limits | [`graphics.md`](graphics.md) |
11-decisions/README.md:243:| G-42 | An `asset` prop in an action's end switches at the action's END, as a string does; `""` names no image in an end (a `null` there removes) and the engine hands `render` `null` for an asset `""`; an asset's start is its string default, or `""`; with an action selected the Graphic tab's image row writes the end, "None" first on every asset row; no format bump; amends G-4, G-34 (b), (d), (l) and G-41 (b), (d) | [`graphics.md`](graphics.md) |
11-decisions/README.md:244:| G-43 | Every colour an action animates blends in OKLab with straight alpha, by key: the nine `[r, g, b, a]` / `video.chroma.key` paths in `video` and `text`, a key whose ends are equal kept exact, inputs clamped to [0, 1], in floating point; one implementation, `model_color.rs`'s unit path, which `oklab_mix` rounds; `oklab.json` gains a third reader; no format bump; amends G-40 (d), G-34 (f) | [`graphics.md`](graphics.md) |

2284 11-decisions/graphics.md

- **G-43 — Every colour an action animates blends in OKLab, with
  straight alpha, by key; amends G-40 (d), G-34 (f)** (graphics gaps
  phase 4, 2026-10-22).
  (a) **The keys.** Nine keys of an action's state are colours, known by
  key and never by the value's shape: `video.shadow.color`, `text.color`,
  `text.outline.color`, `text.backdrop.color`,
  `text.word_style.active_color`, `.spoken_color`, `.upcoming_color`,
  `text.word_style.active_pill.color` (each `[r, g, b, a]`, sRGB-encoded
  0–1) and `video.chroma.key` (`[r, g, b]`, no alpha). Inside the spanning
  action each one whose start and end differ moves from its start toward
  its end in OKLab: the inputs clamped to [0, 1], then G-40's operations
  (sRGB → linear → OKLab, a mix by the eased progress, and back) in
  floating point, never rounded to a byte. Alpha is `a0 + (a1 − a0) × u`,
  straight, never premultiplied, clamped to [0, 1]; the chroma key is rgb
  only. A key whose start and end are the same numbers (compared parsed, so
  a stored `1.0` and an end's `1` are equal) is not blended, so it stays
  exactly as stored (the round trip would drift it by ~1e-7). A value that
  does not read as a colour of its key's arity (a `null`, a missing
  group, a wrong length, a non-number) keeps §5.4's rule: it holds and
  switches at the end. The ends are the stored values: an action's first
  tick is its start and its end is its end, exactly. Red to blue halfway
  is `#8c53a2` (×255 rounded), never `[0.5, 0, 0.5]`.
  (b) **One implementation.** `model_color.rs`'s unit path
  (`oklab_mix_unit`, `oklab_mix_rgb`) is the blend; G-40's `oklab_mix`
  is that path with each byte read as byte/255 and each unit rounded to
  the nearest byte, so its output does not change by a byte.
  `graphic/tests/oklab.json` is answered by three readers:
  `graphic/tests/stdlib.rs`, `core/tests/graphic_actions.rs` (bytes), and
  `core/tests/action_colours.rs`, which takes each case's bytes/255 in and
  compares the result ×255 rounded to the fixture.
  (c) **Older projects** re-render with the new middle. No persisted
  shape changes, so `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` is not bumped and there is no
  migration.
  (d) **Not changed.** The `shape` group and `canvas.background` are not
  action targets (§5.4's three groups), so they have no blend; a colour
  plate is a shape. At a `split` the join is exact (`clip_state` either
  side of the cut is equal); inside the head and the tail a sample
  matches the unsplit clip within the matrices' round-trip error (1e-6
  per channel), not exactly.

  Templates" lists exactly the folder's `*.js` files.
EOF

## Adding a graphic

**Insert ▸ Graphic** lists the bundled templates, then **From File…**:

| Item | What you get | Default length |
|---|---|---|
| Bar Chart | A titled bar chart whose bars grow in turn, from comma-separated values and labels | 150 frames |
| Callout | A circle that draws itself on, with an arrow and a label, at a position on the frame | 90 frames |
| Counter | A number counting from one value to another with thousands separators, a prefix and a label | 90 frames |
| Kinetic Type | A sentence shown word by word, each word springing in, with an accent colour | 150 frames |
| Lower Third | A name and subtitle that slide in and fade out, boxed or not, aligned left, centre or right | 150 frames |
| Title Card | A title fitted to the frame and a kicker over a two-colour gradient, fading in and out | 120 frames |
| From File… | Asks for a `.js` module and copies it into the project | the module's own |

Each template's properties, as the Graphic sub-tab shows them:

| Template | Properties |
|---|---|
| Bar Chart | values and labels (comma-separated text), title, color |
| Callout | x and y (sliders from 0 to 1, a fraction of the frame's width and height), label, color |
| Counter | from, to, prefix, label, color |
| Kinetic Type | text, stagger (1–30), color, accent |
| Lower Third | Title, subtitle, accent, size (12–200), boxed (a checkbox), align (a pop-up: left, center, right) |
| Title Card | title, kicker, from and to (the gradient's two colours) |

Choosing one:

| Item | Shortcut | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Adjustment Clip | | Adds an adjustment clip over the in/out range. Without a range it covers the selected clips' span, and without a selection the whole timeline. Greyed while a nest is open ([Colour grading](color-grading.md)) |
| Graphic ▸ Bar Chart · Callout · Counter · Kinetic Type · Lower Third · Title Card | | Adds a clip made from one of the bundled graphic templates ([Graphics](graphics.md)) |
| Graphic ▸ From File… | | Adds a graphic from a `.js` file you choose |

*Agents:* `add_adjustment_clip`, and `write_graphic` followed by
`add_graphic_clip`.

- **Do:** Open a COPY of `~/temp/testmotiongraphics/parive-promo.framejob` and play its `section` scene (clip 8, from 41.87 s) for 10 s, then play the same 10 s again, then close the window.
- **Expect:** the replay stutters visibly less than the first play. Frame Job's memory stays raised after the plays, at most a quarter of physical memory above the start, and falls when the window closes.
- **Answer:** smoother, yes or no; the memory figure before, after both plays, and after the close.
- **Source:** #127 G6 phase 3 (spec §11 G-37); `tools/proof/graphic_memory_proof.py --bench` measures the share of frames composed on each play, not how the replay looks.

**GR-11 — Background render draws while Frame Job is left alone, and stops when you touch it**
- **Setup:** GR-9's, with Background render on at 5 s in Settings ▸ Playback, and Activity Monitor showing Frame Job's CPU and memory.
- **Do:** Open a COPY of `~/temp/testmotiongraphics/parive-promo.framejob`, park the playhead at 41.87 s, and leave Frame Job alone for 20 s. Press Shift once, wait 20 s, then play 10 s. Park at 41.87 s again, press ⌘H to hide Frame Job and wait 20 s with it hidden. Then show it, untick Background render and leave Frame Job alone for 20 s.
- **Expect:** CPU stays low for about 5 s after you stop, then rises, and falls at the Shift. Hidden, the CPU rises about 5 s after the ⌘H and stays up (a pass opts out of App Nap). Memory stays within a quarter of physical memory above the start. The play is visibly smoother than GR-9's first play. With the box unticked, the CPU stays low while Frame Job is idle.
- **Answer:** CPU low, then up, then down at the Shift, yes or no; smoother than GR-9's first play, yes or no; CPU up while hidden, yes or no; idle CPU low with the box off, yes or no; the memory figure before and at its highest.
- **Source:** #127 G6 phase 4 (spec §11 G-38); `tools/proof/background_render_proof.py` measures this by tool, not the keyboard path or the look.

**GR-12 — A dark gradient graphic shows no rings and no visible grain**
- **Setup:** a 1920×1080 project; your usual display brightness; View ▸ Preview Quality ▸ Full.
- **Do:** Insert ▸ Graphic ▸ From File… a module that fills the frame with a dark radial gradient, e.g. `raster_dither_proof.py`'s `band374` (`<radialGradient gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse" cx="960" cy="540" r="1100">`, `#2A4F3D` at the centre to `#0D1512` at the edge). Look at it in the preview, then save the frame (File ▸ Save Frame… as PNG) and open it in Preview at 100 %. Export it as `prores_422` and as `hevc_10bit`, and once as `h264`, and look at each in QuickTime Player at 100 %.
- **Expect:** in the preview, the saved PNG, the ProRes and the `hevc_10bit` file the gradient shades smoothly, with no rings or steps you can pick out, and no grain you can see at 100 % from your normal distance. The `h264` file may show its steps again: that is PR-13's recorded limit, not a defect.
- **Answer:** rings in the preview, yes or no; rings in the PNG, the ProRes, the `hevc_10bit`, the `h264`, each yes or no; visible grain anywhere, yes or no (and where).
- **Source:** #375 part 1 (spec §11 PR-13); `tools/proof/raster_dither_proof.py` measures the banding (B1–B4b) and the per-pixel noise each export keeps, not how it looks to a person on a display.
